## Installation

You can install the development version of mapuce.data.2020 like so:

``` r
remotes::install_github("AcidyBee/mapuce.data.2020")
```

## Example

Data for this project are agregated at what Insee calls cantville granularity: it corresponds to:
- IRIS for dense areas
- COMMUNE or CANTON for lesser population areas

The atome_indcvi key has been created to link semantic and spatial information for Insee RP indcvi detail files. The atome_indcvi variable is the smallest possible entity for indcvi files, and is obtained using hierachically (IRIS < COMMUNE < CANTON) the information available for each observation in the file.

This is a basic example which shows you how to load data:

```{r example}
library(mapuce.data.2020)
## basic example code
```

### Semantic data

Head of semantic data for zone A: Ile de France. The rows correspond to the city of Paris.

You can see that for the 6 first rows of the dataset, the 9 digits iris_code is available. On the other hand, for Paris the cv_code (cantville) is not complete: it corresponds to the DEPARTEMENT granularity. It is replaced with arm_code which only exists for the 3 major french cities: Lyon, Marseille and Paris).

```{r}
head(mapuce_indcvi_za)
```

### Spatial data

Corresponding choroplethe map data for zone A (Ile de France)

```{r}
spatial_atome_indcvi_za %>% 
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(fill = .data$atome_indcvi_type)) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf() +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = spatial_iris %>% dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(.data$iris_code, "^75")), 
                   linetype = "dotted", linewidth = .15, fill = NA, color = "white") +
  ggplot2::coord_sf() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Frontières atome_indcvi et iris pour l'IdF")
```

...and a zoom for Paris

```{r}
spatial_atome_indcvi_za %>% 
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(.data$atome_indcvi, "^75")) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(fill = .data$atome_indcvi_type)) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf() +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = spatial_iris %>% dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(.data$iris_code, "^75")), 
                   linetype = "dotted", linewidth = .15, fill = NA, color = "white") +
  ggplot2::coord_sf() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Frontières atome_indcvi et iris pour l'IdF")
```
